issue.title: Desktop: production app asks for the browser-tab microphone (ENABLE TAB AUDIO banner) instead of using a native mic

nextActions: Review the reported behavior and build instructions; define the baseline failure before cloning or scheduling a build.
limitations: READY_TO_INVESTIGATE means metadata is sufficient to begin engineering review, not a reproduced or repaired bug.
Dependency manifests are scanned heuristically; transitive dependencies, availability of registry packages, native libraries and physical equipment are not verified.
Only explicit PR references are matched; semantically related work without links can be missed.
Runtime compatibility, contribution policy and complete reproduction steps still require engineering review.

dimensions.reason: The packaged desktop app asks for browser microphone permission instead of using native audio.
The owner opened the issue today.
The reporter is the repository owner and supplied the exact persisted value and desired migration.
Native builds must map browser input/output to system devices while web deployments retain browser choices.
The defect is reproduced by loading or posting browser audio choices under the native flag.
The repair is confined to launch identity, settings migration and guards, status, and picker presentation.
Backend and UI behavior run without physical hardware; the owner can confirm packaged-app microphone selection.
Native and web paths have separate regression assertions.
evidence: Native migration and web preservation tests

dimensions.reason: The owner filed this release-blocking issue against the active 3.0 work today.
The repair prevents a confusing permission prompt and restores expected desktop microphone behavior.
The native/web separation covers input, output, saved settings, and future settings requests.
Correct native capture removes the misleading tab-audio banner and enables downstream speech recognition.

ranking.deliveryNote: Readiness is an evidence-based human assessment, not a calibrated probability. Unknown inputs are never scored as facts.
